config.hypothesis: On a rotated surface code under code-capacity depolarizing noise at p=0.05, dual-decoder coarse-grained virtual error cancellation (MWPM real-time + exact maximum-likelihood offline, Eqs. 10-11 of arXiv:2610.12400) reduces the residual logical bias by at least 10x relative to plain MWPM decoding and is strictly lower than agreement postselection, at a sampling overhead below the paper's standard logical-PEC benchmark (eta < 4).

upstream.paper: Shtanko, Roy, Kumar, Minev (Google Quantum AI), "Measure Now, Mitigate Later: Virtual Error Cancellation for Logical Quantum Circuits", arXiv:2610.12400 (CC BY 4.0). No official code; this is an independent re-implementation.

equations.noise: E_p(rho) = (1-p) rho + p/3 (X rho X + Y rho Y + Z rho Z) per data qubit
equations.sectors: S_Q = { s : D_rt(s) * D_off(s) ~ Q }, Q in {I,X,Y,Z}  (Eq. 10)
equations.offline_decoder: exact coset partition functions Z_L(s) (Eq. S.1), here by exhaustive 4^9 enumeration (d=3) and an exact transfer-matrix contraction with bond dimension <= 2^d x 4 (d=5,7), verified against brute force at d=3 to max |diff| ~ 1e-15 (src/verify.py).

noise.model: code-capacity depolarizing, one perfect syndrome-extraction round
noise.simulator: stim detector sampler; the true logical frame flip Q' is recorded through a noiseless reference ancilla (Bell-paired logical observables), used for BENCHMARKING AND ORACLE CALIBRATION ONLY, as in the paper's Fig. 2 benchmark (Supplementary Sec. II.A). Disclosure: the main experiment is oracle-calibrated (sector centroids from true frame flips on the calibration split), like the paper's Fig. 2; the syndrome-only noise-learning path (Eqs. 16-17) is a report-only stretch breakpoint.

decoders.real_time: PyMatching MWPM on decoupled X/Z graphs, weights ln[(1-q)/q], q=2p/3
decoders.offline: exact ML over the four logical cosets (see offline_decoder above)
decoders.d5_decision: DECIDED PRE-REGISTRATION: exact d=5 ML runs in budget (verified 0.003 ms/syndrome, src/verify.py), so the primary claim covers d=3 AND d=5. d=7 is included as report-only (seed 0 only, smaller shots).

seeding.note: calibration and eval sampling are independent streams per seed

metrics.primary: p_res = || sum_k q_k w_k p_k ||_1 (residual logical Pauli error, L1) on HELD-OUT eval shots, with weights fitted on the separate calibration set; per seed. Baselines on the same eval shots: plain decoding (w = 1, p_res = p_L_MWPM) and agreement postselection (w_Q = 0, renormalised, p_res = ||p_I||_1).
metrics.statistical_floor: 1-sigma floor on p_res must sit well below 0.1*p_L. With n_eval = 1e6 (d=3) the per-component shot-noise floor is ~sqrt(C*p_bar/N) ~ 3e-4 against 0.1*p_L ~ 3e-3 (p_L ~ 3e-2 at d=3, p=0.05); with n_eval = 5e5 (d=5) it is ~2e-4 against 0.1*p_L ~ 1.5e-3. Error bars: paired delete-1 jackknife over B=20 shards (cal and eval shards dropped jointly).
metrics.observable_check: report estimated <Z_L> on |0_L> and <X_L> on |+_L> (ideal +1) for plain / postselect / VEC with jackknife CIs (report-only).
report_only: MWPM vs ML logical error rate

thresholds.pass_condition:
For d=3 AND d=5, on EVERY seed in {0,1,2}:
  (1) p_res_VEC <= 0.1 * p_L_MWPM   (same seed, eval split),
  (2) p_res_VEC <  p_res_postselect (same seed, eval split),
  (3) eta_VEC = (C - 1)/p_L_MWPM < 4.
thresholds.status_rule: PASS if all three conditions hold on all seeds for both d=3 and d=5. PARTIAL if VEC beats postselection and plain decoding on all seeds (conditions (2) and p_res_VEC < p_L_MWPM) but misses the 10x or eta<4 bar. FAIL otherwise.

p_sweep.story: where VEC's advantage and eta break down toward/above threshold

cal_budget.story: p_res vs calibration size, from official cal shard prefixes (seed 0)

drift.story: weights calibrated at p=0.05 applied at every p' in p_values

weight_sweep.story: residual vs one contested weight w_Q (X and Y sectors), consensus weight adjusted to keep sum q_k w_k = 1 (paper Fig. 2d convention); minimum at w_Q* vs postselection (w_Q=0) and no mitigation (w_Q=1).

runtime.paper_reference_point: QUOTED from arXiv:2610.12400 (Supp. Sec. II.B), NOT claimed reproduced here (paper value is at d=7): at d=7, p=0.05 the paper reports P_XX ~ P_ZZ ~ 0.86, P_YY ~ 0.78, w_I* ~ 1.01, w_X* = w_Z* ~ -0.42, w_Y* ~ -4e-2. Our d=7 report-only run is compared against these numbers.

config.disclosure: Thresholds and shot counts fixed before the official run. The only pre-registration computation was src/verify.py (decoder correctness + timing, no hypothesis metrics) and one smoke (2e4 shots, seed 0; recorded in smoke.json and results.md). No threshold was changed after any result. Oracle calibration disclosure: sector shares/centroids are estimated from true frame flips on the calibration split, exactly like the paper's Fig. 2 benchmark; the noise-learning breakpoint uses no true labels.
